![ISO thread SCAD library by flipmarley | Download free STL ...](data:image/png;base64,)

OpenSCAD threading libraries like [threads-scad](https://github.com/rcolyer/threads-scad) and [BOSL2's threading module](https://github.com/revarbat/BOSL2/wiki/threading.scad) ==provide parametric tools to generate 3D-printable screws, bolts, nuts, and custom threaded rods==. [[1](https://github.com/rcolyer/threads-scad), [2](https://github.com/revarbat/BOSL2/wiki/threading.scad)]

Popular OpenSCAD Threading Options

- **`threads-scad` (`rcolyer`)**: Generates efficient metric-compatible threads, hex nuts, bolts, washers, and auger threads as single polyhedrons using list comprehensions for fast rendering. Ideal for reliable M2+ internal and M4+ external 3D printed threads. [[1](https://github.com/rcolyer/threads-scad/blob/master/README.md), [2](https://github.com/rcolyer/threads-scad)]
- **`BOSL2` (`threading.scad`)**: Part of the comprehensive BOSL2 library, supporting standard triangular (ISO/UTS), trapezoidal (ACME), square, and pipe threads with advanced attachment and tolerance controls (`$slop`). [[1](https://github.com/revarbat/BOSL2/wiki/threading.scad)]
- **`threadlib` (`adrianschlatter`)**: Offers extensive metric, unified inch (UNC/UNF), and BSP parallel thread tables with production tolerances and custom pitch support. [[1](https://github.com/adrianschlatter/threadlib)]
- **Classic `threads.scad` (`verhas`)**: A traditional library by Dan Kirshner supporting ISO metric and English threads with square or rectangular profiles. [[1](https://github.com/verhas/OpenScad/blob/main/threads.scad)]

Basic Usage Example (`threads-scad`)

openscad

```
include <threads-scad/threads.scad>

// Create a standard metric bolt (e.g., M8, 20mm long)
MetricBolt(diameter=8, length=20);

// Create a matching nut
translate([15, 0, 0])
MetricNut(diameter=8, thickness=6);
```

Use code with caution.

## You said: I'm designing a miniature cylybdrical box for resin printing that uses a thread to close the box.

I'm designing a miniature cylybdrical box for resin printing that uses a thread to close the box.

October 3, 2026

Designing a miniature cylindrical box with threads for resin printing is ==highly rewarding because **SLA/DLP resin printers excel at high-detail, small-scale threads**==. However, resin tends to expand slightly due to light bleed (curing slightly beyond the pixel boundaries) and shrinks during post-curing. [[1](https://jlc3dp.com/help/article/3d-printing-design-guideline), [2](https://sinterit.com/3d-printing-guide/design-for-3d-printing/tolerances-3d-printing/), [3](https://www.reddit.com/r/resinprinting/comments/tkhxsi/tolerances_to_add_for_resin_printing/), [4](https://www.jcproto.com/new/3d-printing-threads-tolerance.html)]

To compensate for this, you need an intentional **clearance gap (manufacturing offset)** between your container's male and female threads. The **[BOSL2 library](https://github.com/revarbat/BOSL2/wiki/threading.scad)** is strongly recommended for this task because it features a built-in variable `$slop` specifically designed to automatically expand internal threads for a perfect fit. [[1](https://github.com/revarbat/BOSL2/wiki/threading.scad), [2](https://www.jcproto.com/new/3d-printing-threads-tolerance.html)]

OpenSCAD Code (BOSL2)

openscad

```
include <BOSL2/std.scad>
include <BOSL2/threading.scad>

// --- CUSTOMIZATION PARAMETERS ---
$fn = 64;                 // Smoothness of circles
box_outer_d = 25;         // Outer diameter of the box (miniature)
box_height = 30;          // Total internal depth/height of the base
wall_thickness = 2;       // Side wall thickness

thread_d = 21;            // Outer diameter of the thread (must clear wall thickness)
thread_pitch = 1.5;       // Pitch in mm (1.5mm is great for miniature resin boxes)
thread_h = 6;             // Height of the threaded section

// RESIN PRINTER CLEARANCE SETTING
// $slop adds radial clearance to internal (female) threads automatically.
// For resin printing, a total clearance of 0.2mm to 0.4mm works best.
// BOSL2 scales internal threads by (4 * $slop), so $slop = 0.075 gives a ~0.3mm total gap.
$slop = 0.075;

// --- RENDERING CONTROL ---
// Toggle between viewing the "base", "lid", or "both"
render_mode = "both";

if (render_mode == "base" || render_mode == "both") {
    color("LightBlue") box_base();
}

if (render_mode == "lid" || render_mode == "both") {
    // Lift the lid up in "both" view to inspect the threads
    translate([0, 0, (render_mode == "both") ? box_height + 15 : 0])
        color("Tomato") box_lid();
}

// --- MODULES ---

module box_base() {
    difference() {
        // Main outer body
        cylinder(d=box_outer_d, h=box_height, anchor=BOTTOM);

        // Internal storage cavity
        translate([0, 0, wall_thickness])
            cylinder(d=box_outer_d - (wall_thickness * 2), h=box_height, anchor=BOTTOM);

        // Internal Thread (Female) cut out of the top rim
        translate([0, 0, box_height - thread_h])
            threaded_rod(d=thread_d, pitch=thread_pitch, l=thread_h+0.1, internal=true, anchor=BOTTOM);
    }
}

module box_lid() {
    // Lid Cap
    cylinder(d=box_outer_d, h=wall_thickness + 1, anchor=BOTTOM);

    // Male Thread protruding down from the lid cap
    translate([0, 0, wall_thickness + 1])
        threaded_rod(d=thread_d, pitch=thread_pitch, l=thread_h, internal=false, anchor=BOTTOM);
}
```

Use code with caution.

Essential Design Tips for Resin-Printed Threads

1. **Keep the Pitch Coarse:** For miniature items, avoid tiny pitches (like 0.5mm or 0.75mm). Liquid resin can get trapped in the microscopic grooves via capillary action and cure solid. Stick to a **1.5mm or 2mm pitch**, which allows excess resin to wash away easily. [[1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eBte6lmHzOc)]
2. **Orient to Avoid Suction Cups:** If you print the box base flat on the build plate right-side up, it becomes a "suction cup" trapping resin during lifts. Print the base flipped upside down (resting on its rim with supports), or tilt it at a **30° to 45° angle** with heavy support structures to allow the resin to drain cleanly out of the threads.
3. **Bevel/Chamfer the Thread Intros:** To prevent cross-threading and help the lid smoothly align when you close it, ensure your model has chamfers at the lips. `BOSL2` automatically applies a slight lead-in bevel to the `threaded_rod()` endpoints by default. [[1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6brs9KcoyMs&t=715), [2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7YAylxQFe3k&t=98), [3](https://gitgud.io/popnil/bosl2/-/blob/master/threading.scad)]
4. **Post-Processing Care:** Thoroughly wash the threads with fresh Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) and scrub them gently with a soft toothbrush before UV curing. If you don't clean the thread valleys properly, any remaining liquid film will cure hard and permanently ruin the fit. [[1](https://www.jcproto.com/new/3d-printing-threads-tolerance.html)]

## You said: Yes, do it

Yes, do it

October 3, 2026

Here is the updated OpenSCAD code featuring a knurled texture (grip ridges) on both the lid and the base.

Because `BOSL2` includes powerful built-in texturing tools, we can easily add vertical grip grooves around the cylinder walls without slowing down the OpenSCAD renderer.

OpenSCAD Code with Grip Ridges

openscad

```
include <BOSL2/std.scad>
include <BOSL2/threading.scad>
include <BOSL2/masks.scad>

// --- CUSTOMIZATION PARAMETERS ---
$fn = 64;                 // Smoothness of circles
box_outer_d = 25;         // Outer diameter of the box (miniature)
box_height = 30;          // Total internal depth/height of the base
wall_thickness = 2;       // Side wall thickness

thread_d = 21;            // Outer diameter of the thread (must clear wall thickness)
thread_pitch = 1.5;       // Pitch in mm (1.5mm is great for miniature resin boxes)
thread_h = 6;             // Height of the threaded section

// GRIP / KNURLING SETTINGS
ridge_count = 24;         // Number of vertical grooves around the perimeter
ridge_depth = 0.6;        // How deep the grip grooves cut into the walls

// RESIN PRINTER CLEARANCE SETTING
// $slop adds radial clearance to internal (female) threads automatically.
// For resin printing, a total clearance of 0.2mm to 0.4mm works best.
// BOSL2 scales internal threads by (4 * $slop), so $slop = 0.075 gives a ~0.3mm total gap.
$slop = 0.075;

// --- RENDERING CONTROL ---
// Toggle between viewing the "base", "lid", or "both"
render_mode = "both";

if (render_mode == "base" || render_mode == "both") {
    color("LightBlue") box_base();
}

if (render_mode == "lid" || render_mode == "both") {
    // Lift the lid up in "both" view to inspect the threads
    translate([0, 0, (render_mode == "both") ? box_height + 15 : 0])
        color("Tomato") box_lid();
}

// --- MODULES ---

module box_base() {
    difference() {
        // Main outer body
        cylinder(d=box_outer_d, h=box_height, anchor=BOTTOM);

        // Vertical grip ridges cut into the outer wall
        grip_ridges(h=box_height);

        // Internal storage cavity
        translate([0, 0, wall_thickness])
            cylinder(d=box_outer_d - (wall_thickness * 2), h=box_height, anchor=BOTTOM);

        // Internal Thread (Female) cut out of the top rim
        translate([0, 0, box_height - thread_h])
            threaded_rod(d=thread_d, pitch=thread_pitch, l=thread_h+0.1, internal=true, anchor=BOTTOM);
    }
}

module box_lid() {
    lid_cap_h = wall_thickness + 1;

    difference() {
        // Lid Cap
        cylinder(d=box_outer_d, h=lid_cap_h, anchor=BOTTOM);

        // Vertical grip ridges cut into the lid cap outer wall
        grip_ridges(h=lid_cap_h);
    }

    // Male Thread protruding down from the lid cap
    translate([0, 0, lid_cap_h])
        threaded_rod(d=thread_d, pitch=thread_pitch, l=thread_h, internal=false, anchor=BOTTOM);
}

// Helper module to generate even spacing for grip cuts
module grip_ridges(h) {
    for (i = [0 : ridge_count - 1]) {
        rotate([0, 0, i * (360 / ridge_count)])
            translate([box_outer_d / 2, 0, -0.1])
                // Triangular shape cutting into the side wall
                cylinder(d1=ridge_depth*2, d2=ridge_depth*2, h=h+0.2, $fn=3, anchor=BOTTOM);
    }
}
```

Use code with caution.

What Changed?

- **`grip_ridges()` module:** This dynamically calculates a radial array of small triangular cuts that slice into the outermost edge of both your base and lid.
- **Tactile and Aesthetic Utility:** This gives your resin-printed box a highly functional texture that looks modern and gives your fingers enough traction to easily twist a tiny lid off a tiny base.

Pro Resin Tip for Textured Prints

When cleaning this print in your wash station, make sure to give the outer ridges a quick pass with a soft brush. Uncured resin easily pools inside tiny aesthetic grooves like these, and if it cures inside them, it can flatten out your grip design and make it look muddy.
